elements.element: If the agreement does not use automatic renewal, each renewal requires mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause uses automatic renewal, so the condition for this alternative is absent; the mutual-written-agreement branch is therefore inapplicable.

elements.element: If the agreement uses automatic renewal, each renewal term is 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides for automatic renewal for “additional 1-year terms.”

elements.element: If the agreement uses automatic renewal, Customer may opt out on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Customer must provide sixty (60) days' written notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: If the agreement uses automatic renewal, Vendor must provide Customer a reminder 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal-reminder obligation is imposed on Kubient.

elements.element: Any price increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Neither the renewal clause nor the fees provision contains a price-increase cap tied to CPI or 3%.
The clause states that the Agreement “will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms.”

elements.element: Customer may elect non-renewal on no more than 60 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate for any reason following the Initial Term on sixty (60) days' written notice. This rolling termination right is at least as protective as a 60-day non-renewal right because notice may be used to make termination effective at the end of the Initial Term or a renewal term.

elements.element: Any price increase is capped at 5%.
elements.evidence: No provision limits price increases to 5% or less.

result.reason: The redline establishes automatic one-year renewals and reduces Customer's exit notice to 60 days, but it omits every price-increase cap. It also lacks the preferred 30-day Customer notice and Vendor renewal reminder. Because no complete preferred or fallback level is achieved, the redline is not minimal under the stated definition, notwithstanding that its only substantive change is directionally relevant. Unrelated commercial terms remain operative and no contradiction is introduced.
